content: AP4M1, also known as AP-4 complex subunit mu-1, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the AP4M1 gene. Function The AP4M1 gene encodes a subunit of the heterotetrameric AP-4 complex. The protein produced by this gene is a member of the adaptor complexes medium subunits family. The AP-4 complex is specifically involved in the recognition and sorting of cargo proteins that contain tyrosine-based motifs. This sorting process occurs as these cargo proteins are transported from the trans-Golgi network to the endosomal-lysosomal system. Interactions The AP4M1 protein has been demonstrated to interact with another protein, AP4B1, which is a component of the same AP-4 complex. Clinical Relevance The trafficking mediated by the AP-4 complex is essential for proper brain development and functioning. Disruptions in this process can have significant implications for neurological health.
